title: Decision-level routing observability: decision logs, per-hop metrics & trace linking
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add end-to-end observability for smart routing decisions so engineers and SREs can answer: why was a request routed to region X or tier Y, when did fallback to a model variant occur, and what was the per-hop latency breakdown? Deliverables include a decision-log schema, trace/span linking for routing hops, per-hop metrics instrumentation, Console dashboards, and queryable storage with retention policy. Must exclude prompt contents and PII, support sampling policies, and be safe for high-throughput production traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Decision log schema documented and reviewed in Confluence with fields: decision_id, request_id, timestamp, client_region, chosen_region, routing_tier, fallback_variant, reason_code, variant_latency_ms, total_routing_latency_ms, trace_id, span_id, sampling_rate, model_id, token_count; no prompt text or user PII stored.
Runtime emits decision log events to the routing Kafka topic (routing.decisions) for 100% of error/fallback cases and 5% of successful fast-path cases; sampling is configurable via feature flag.
Each routing hop creates a span linked to the overall request trace; traces visible in existing tracing backend and correlated to decision logs by trace_id.
Per-hop metrics (enqueue_ms, dispatch_ms, model_infer_ms, network_ms) emitted to metric system with tags: region, tier, model_variant, customer_tier, decision_reason.

Console surfaces a new Routing Decisions dashboard: aggregated fallback rates by region/tier, per-hop latency percentiles, and a trace+decision lookup UI; queries return results under 5s for 30d retention.
Privacy check completed: audit confirms no prompt content, only model_id and token_count are stored; security signoff recorded in ticket comments.
Canary rollout plan executed: instrumentation behind feature flag and enabled for internal orgs before wider enablement.
implementation_notes: Schema proposal posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/routing-decision-schema (draft). Use snake_case field names to match existing logging conventions.

Event pipeline: runtime -> routing.kafka.producer -> streams -> clickhouse(routing_decisions) and a low-latency materialized view for Console queries. Consider parquet export to s3 for long-term retention.
Sampling: implement deterministic sampling by client_id hash for non-error traffic; always sample all fallback/error decisions and requests tagged with customer_impact=high.
Trace linking: add trace_id/span_id to decision log, create a short-lived routing span for each policy evaluation hop; instrument with opentracing-compatible headers used by our observability stack.

Per-hop metrics: emit timers per hop with tags for hop_index, policy_type (region_select|tier_route|fallback), chosen_node, and model_variant. Use histogram buckets aligned with existing latency SLOs.
Privacy: do not capture prompt text or embeddings. Add a scrubber that strips any user-provided metadata fields that look like emails/SSNs before writing to logs.
Storage & retention: routing_decisions table TTL 90 days; materialized view for Console 30 days. Cost estimate attached in comments.
Feature flag: runtime.flag.routing_observability with per-org whitelist for rollout. Default off for public tenants until privacy & cost signoffs complete.
Backfill: small backfill utility to populate clickhouse for last 7 days from Kafka if needed for dashboards; limited to internal orgs only.

Docs: update runbooks and docs for incident triage using decision logs (DX)

Small backfill utility and migration plan (ENG infra)
